text:
maria: Heads-up - since the OFED + firmware push to eu-central yesterday evening we're seeing a sustained drop in NCCL allreduce bandwidth on a small subset of nodes (p100s and a couple of a100s in rack r15).

akshay: Confirmed. Alerts from perf-dash show 60-75% throughput vs baseline for several jobs. Latency spikes around 25-40% too.

chip: Any packet drops on the IB interfaces? run `ifconfig`/`ethtool` or `perfquery` yet?

maria: ran a quick `ethtool -S mlx5_core` on affected hosts, nothing obvious on CRC/errs. But tcp fallback events in the NCCL logs: `transport: falling back to TCP` repeated.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: OFED v5.2.1 + mlx5-firmware 1.2.3 rolled out to eu-central-rack-r13..r16 at 2025-11-07T21:40Z.

dimi: If NCCL is falling back to TCP that means the RDMA transport either failed negotiation or QP errors triggered fallback. Can you paste the nccl log snippet?

maria: pasted below: ```
[0] NCCL WARN Transport: ib (rank 2 -> 5) handshake timed out, fallback to TCP
[0] NCCL INFO Bootstrap: using TCP for rank 2 -> 5
[0] NCCL WARN Transport: rdma_connect() returned -110
```

akshay: I grabbed `dmesg` from one of the a100s: `mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: FW error: link packet splitting enabled (quirk) - resetting queues` followed by a lot of retries.

chip: packet splitting? firmware change must have toggled segmentation offload or steering that our NIC drivers expect. That can cause QP handshake failures.

grace: Impacted jobs are mostly high-throughput training and some internal evals. We've queued 3 job cancellations to free capacity, but cost and deadlines will slip if this persists.

maria: Quick reproduction: forced two-node allreduce between two affected hosts. Repro: bandwidth drop from ~120Gb/s to ~20-30Gb/s and NCCL logs show repeated rdma_connect errors then fallback.

dimi: Can we isolate to firmware vs OFED? Any hosts still on old firmware?

maria: Yes, rack r12 still on previous firmware + OFED (not yet upgraded). Cross-testing shows r12 <-> r15 uses RDMA fine; r15 <-> r15 fails. So points to firmware/driver mismatch on upgraded hosts.

akshay: Rolling back firmware across a bunch of hosts is painful. Short-term mitigation: force NCCL to prefer GDR or set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1? That would degrade performance but avoid TCP fallback loop.

chip: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 disables IB path and forces TCP — that's worse. We want to force use of RoCE v2 settings or disable firmware's packet-splitting feature. Is there a mlx5 module param to toggle TSO/packet-splitting?

maria: There's a driver param `mlx5_core.pkt_split` (0/1/2) on some distros. On these nodes it was auto-set by firmware and the vendor driver combo. I can try toggling to 0 on one node for testing.

infra-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/efa-deploy-rollback (requires SSO)

maria: toggled `mlx5_core.pkt_split=0` and reloaded module on node r15n3. Re-ran allreduce: bandwidth recovered to ~110Gb/s and no TCP fallback in logs.

dimi: Great repro and narrow scope. So firmware introduced pkt-split behavior incompatible with our NCCL/OFED stack.

grace: What's the blast radius? How many nodes have the new firmware?

maria: infra-bot said racks r13..r16 (~48 hosts) were updated. I'll run a quick inventory and mark them in the incident doc.

akshay: Plan suggestion: 1) Pin firmware on remaining racks to previous version, 2) set `pkt_split=0` via kernel module parameter for affected hosts as stopgap, 3) coordinate with vendor for proper firmware fix, 4) schedule controlled firmware rollout with validation tests.

chip: Also add a health-check in deploy pipeline that runs a tiny nccl allreduce (1s) between two upgraded hosts post-firmware; fail the rollout if fallback occurs.

maria: I've applied `modprobe -r mlx5_core && modprobe mlx5_core pkt_split=0` across all affected hosts and pushing a daisy-chain validation. So far 30/48 updated and passing.

dimi: What's the ops cost? We're canceling / rescheduling training, slack notices to customers?

grace: Cost hit is moderate - a handful of high-priority jobs timed out and will rerun, impacting GPU hour burn. I'm documenting for support billing review.

akshay: Long-term we should pin a compat matrix of firmware + OFED + kernel + NCCL we test against, and bake into the deploy pipeline. This reaffirms the need for preflight integration tests.

maria: I'll open a vendor ticket with logs and the firmware fingerprint. Also opening a postmortem ticket and scheduling a rollback window for any hosts that didn't get the module param toggled.

chip: Thanks team. If vendor provides fixed firmware, we will coordinate a staged rollout with the NCCL smoke check. Until then keep `pkt_split=0` as default on eu-central nodes.

grace: I'm pinging product and support for customer impact comms.

maria: tagging owners: @dimi (platform), @chip (network), @grace (support), will update thread with vendor reply. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident-created: INC-2025-4187 (link)
